label: reported (public sources), not measured by us
what_this_is: Water-logging (water-clogging) hotspots on or next to the Lingampally -> Lakdikapul corridor, taken from public reports (GHMC / HYDRAA hotspot lists, traffic police rain advisories, newspapers). Each point is tied to the nearest corridor junction (data/corridor/corridor.json). We have not measured any of this ourselves.
how_the_simulation_uses_it: In a rain what-if (POST /corridor/runs {weather}), every road lane within radius_m of a reported junction (the corridor approaching and leaving it, and its cross arms; not a flyover deck above it) gets an extra speed cap: cap x extra_speed_factor[weather][severity]. This comes ON TOP of the per-stretch rain factors in data/rain/rain_factors.json. No double counting: the stretch factor is the measured average rain effect over a whole leg (TomTom hourly x Open-Meteo, July 2026); the junction factor is the extra, local slowdown where water collects, which the leg average hides. Both are relative to the run's own calibration.

extra_speed_factor.label: assumed, scaled by reported severity
extra_speed_factor.note: Heavy rain: every reported point floods (high / medium / low). Light rain: only the chronic (high) points, at half the heavy-rain effect. Nobody has measured these factors; they are a reading of the reports (knee-deep water and stranded vehicles = high).

severity_meaning.high: repeated reports of deep water, stranded vehicles or road closed; on an official hotspot list
severity_meaning.medium: water-logging that slows traffic, in more than one report
